long_biography.plain_text:
Howalt studied at Boston University and served in the Army Air Corps before joining Tillotson Rubber in the late 1940s. Neil Tillotson became his mentor, father-in-law and long-term business partner, giving the young salesman technical grounding and an experienced industry counterpart. With Tillotson's financial backing, Howalt moved to northwest Georgia and started TRCC, selling latex and providing hands-on service to carpet producers.

He grew the company through professional managers, international facilities and acquisitions, extending its chemistry beyond flooring into water treatment, mining, personal care, medical devices, paper, lubricants and coatings. Delegating responsibility also left room for serious offshore sailing, a pursuit that reinforced his preference for capable, trusted operating teams. Howalt remained founder-chairman of a privately held manufacturing group that continued under later leadership after his death in 2021.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative input links person 1058 to Abide. The Cruising Club identifies F. Harvey Howalt of Dalton with the 140-foot Jongert Islandia, and YachtBuyer records Abide as the current name of the 41.45-metre Jongert launched as Islandia. The metre and rounded-foot measurements align, making the bridge very strong, but the public sources are not beneficial-ownership registries. Vessel context is used only to resolve identity and is excluded from both biographies.

The source record still marks Howalt Alive, but an exact family obituary and contemporaneous flooring-industry notice establish his death on 6 July 2021. The dossier proposes correcting mortality to Deceased. Day, month, year and calculated age 94 are preserved as dependent review candidates because the inventory currently classifies death fields as inapplicable until that correction is accepted.

The immutable input labels Abide as Howalt's current vessel from 1999, yet he died in 2021 and public yacht material describes a later refit and current status. The dossier does not assert post-death ownership, transfer the present yacht to his estate, or propose a vessel change; it flags the source relationship as likely historical or stale.

The obituary uses F. Harvey Howalt Jr. and explains that his father was Frederick Harvey Howalt Sr. Harvey was therefore the public middle-name form of Frederick Harvey Howalt Jr., but the authoritative record stores Harvey as the first name. The dossier proposes the directly supported Jr. suffix without restructuring the first and middle names or replacing the established display name.

The obituary says Howalt spent his early years in the Boston area but does not explicitly say he was born there. Lower-quality biographical databases identify Boston as his birthplace, but that evidence does not meet the strong-source threshold, so place_of_birth remains blank.

FloorDaily says Howalt founded Textile Rubber in 1951, while the family obituary describes the move to Georgia and operating start in 1952 and formal incorporation in 1956. The biographies avoid an exact founding year because the sources appear to use different milestones rather than because the founder identity is in doubt.

Howalt performed the early selling, technical service and operating work and built the enterprise over decades. Neil Tillotson nevertheless provided the relevant industry platform, a latex formulation, mentorship, a 45-year partnership and explicit financial backing. Self-made — advantaged start captures both the founder's achievement and the material family-connected advantage without inventing inheritance.
